hintHtml:
Format of the required email notification. Reserved words:{ObjectName} - object

  • {CompanyName} - company
  • {ObjectTypeName} - object type
  • {idXXXX} - request line data
  • {idXXXXp} - request line previous data
  • {RequestID} - request id
  • {RequestDetail,width} or {RequestDetails,width} - request detail (table)
  • {RequestDetailFilter,width} or {RequestDetailsFilter,width} - request detail (table: Create - only entered, Update - only changed)
  • {RoleName} - name of new role
  • {RequestStatus} - request status
  • {NextUserName} - name of new assigned user
  • {PrevUserName} - current user name (who pressed action button)
  • {RequestorName} - name of the requestor
  • {RequestType} - type of request: Create / Update
  • (RequestSubGrid,Width,ObjectLineID,ObjectSubLineID,...} - table with sub-grid on selected fields
  • {RequestComment,width} or {RequestComments,width} - table with request comments of selected width in %
  • {RequestWorkflow,width} - table with request workflow history of selected width in %
hintText: Format of the required email notification. It is defined by attributes:

hintHtml:
Specifies the option that is used for binding to the server.

Select option:

  • Negotiate - The client is authenticated by using either Kerberos or NTLM. When the user name and password are not provided, the Account Management API binds to the object by using the security context of the calling thread, which is either the security context of the user account under which the application is running or of the client user account that the calling thread represents.
  • Sealing - The data is encrypted by using Kerberos.
  • SecureSocketLayer - The channel is encrypted by using the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL). Active Directory requires that the Certificate Services be installed to support SSL.
  • ServerBind - Specify this flag when you use the domain context type if the application is binding to a specific server name.
  • Signing - The integrity of the data is verified. This flag can only be used with the Negotiate context option and is not available with the simple bind option.
  • SimpleBind - The client is authenticated by using the Basic authentication.
hintText: Specifies the option that is used for binding to the server. Select option: Negotiate - The client is authenticated by using either Kerberos or NTLM. When the user name and password are not provided, the Account Management API binds to the object by using the security context of the calling thread, which is either the security context of the user account under which the application is running or of the client user account that the calling thread represents. Sealing - The data is encrypted by using Kerberos. SecureSocketLayer - The channel is encrypted by using the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL). Active Directory requires that the Certificate Services be installed to support SSL. ServerBind - Specify this flag when you use the domain context type if the application is binding to a specific server name. Signing - The integrity of the data is verified. This flag can only be used with the Negotiate context option and is not available with the simple bind option. SimpleBind - The client is authenticated by using the Basic authentication.

hintHtml:
Specifies the option that is used for binding to the server during import of LDAP users.

Select option:

  • Anonymous - No authentication is performed.
  • Delegation - Enables Active Directory Services Interface (ADSI) to delegate the user's security context, which is necessary for moving objects across domains.
  • FastBind - Specifies that ADSI will not attempt to query the Active Directory Domain Services objectClass property. Therefore, only the base interfaces that are supported by all ADSI objects will be exposed. Other interfaces that the object supports will not be available. A user can use this option to boost the performance in a series of object manipulations that involve only methods of the base interfaces. However, ADSI does not verify if any of the request objects actually exist on the server.
  • ReadonlyServer - For a WinNT provider, ADSI tries to connect to a domain controller. For Active Directory Domain Services, this flag indicates that a writable server is not required for a serverless binding.
  • Sealing - Encrypts data using Kerberos. The Secure flag must also be set to use sealing.
  • Secure - Requests secure authentication. When this flag is set, the WinNT provider uses NTLM to authenticate the client. Active Directory Domain Services uses Kerberos, and possibly NTLM, to authenticate the client. When the user name and password are a null reference (Nothing in Visual Basic), ADSI binds to the object using the security context of the calling thread, which is either the security context of the user account under which the application is running or of the client user account that the calling thread is impersonating.
  • SecureSocketsLayer - Attaches a cryptographic signature to the message that both identifies the sender and ensures that the message has not been modified in transit. Active Directory Domain Services requires the Certificate Server be installed to support Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption.
  • ServerBind - If your ADsPath includes a server name, specify this flag when using the LDAP provider. Do not use this flag for paths that include a domain name or for serverless paths. Specifying a server name without also specifying this flag results in unnecessary network traffic.
  • Signing - Verifies data integrity to ensure that the data received is the same as the data sent. The Secure flag must also be set to use signing.

Therefore, only the base interfaces that are supported by all ADSI objects will be exposed. Other interfaces that the object supports will not be available. A user can use this option to boost the performance in a series of object manipulations that involve only methods of the base interfaces. hintHtml:
Under input mask you are able to change mask behaviour. Together with input mask we will be able to define also length of the field.

Input mask is possible only for object type: "Text-box (1 line)", "Text – box (multiline)" and "Number" if autonumber is not selected.

Below table described the possible characters. If in the input mask should be defined fixed text it have to be put into square brackets [text] otherwise should be ignored and removed from input mask in request details.


MandatoryOptional
Number [0-9]9#
Lower case [a-z]ab
Upper case [A-Z]AB
Alfanumeric [a-zA-Z0-9]wx
Any character*%
Emailemail
IBANiban
IP Address (v4)ipv4
Decimal
#.##

Mandatory means that characted have to be entered and Optional means that it can be skipped. Couple of examples:

  • Mask: [ABC]999

Valid input: ABC123, ABC456

Invalid input: ABC1__, ABC25_

  • Mask: [ABC]99###

Valid input: ABC124, ABC45687

Invalid input: ABC1_

  • Mask: wwwwwxxx

Valid input: tomas, tomasbe

Invalid input: toma_, tomasbelak (should not be possible to enter)

  • Mask: ####.##

Valid input: any number between -9999.99 to 9999.99

  • Mask: ##

Valid: any number between -99 to 99

Note: "Any character" can be any printable character as space, asterix, or any other special char.

Couple of examples: Mask: [ABC]999 Valid input: ABC123, ABC456 Invalid input: ABC1__, ABC25_ Mask: [ABC]99### Valid input: ABC124, ABC45687 Invalid input: ABC1_ Mask: wwwwwxxx Valid input: tomas, tomasbe Invalid input: toma_, tomasbelak (should not be possible to enter) Mask: ####.## Valid input: any number between -9999.99 to 9999.99 Mask: ## Valid: any number between -99 to 99 Note: "Any character" can be any printable character as space, asterix, or any other special char.

hintHtml:
Under this field you are able to define Authentication type for user access.

Select option:

  • Local application - this authentication type uses access based on local (Xeelo) authentication values (username,password).
  • External LDAP (login/password) - this authentication type uses access based on LDAP attributes which are defined in the system
  • External LDAP (session) - this authentication type uses access based on session IDs.
hintText: Under this field you are able to define Authentication type for user access. Select option: Local application - this authentication type uses access based on local (Xeelo) authentication values (username,password). External LDAP (login/password) - this authentication type uses access based on LDAP attributes which are defined in the system External LDAP (session) - this authentication type uses access based on session IDs.

hintHtml:
Setup scheduling period for task

ExpressionMeaning
0/30 * * * * ?Fire every 30 seconds
0 0/2 * * * ?Fire every 2 minutes
0 0 12 * * ?Fire at 12pm (noon) every day
0 15 10 * * ?Fire at 10:15am every day
0 15 10 15 * ?Fire at 10:15am on the 15th day of every month

For more examples see Documentation

hintHtml:
Set object line mode to horizontal

  • true – when object line has IsLabel flag set, label is show left to the object line content (except SubGrid line - label is always show in the header place of SubGrid)
  • false – when object line has IsLabel flag set, label is show above the object line content (except SubGrid line - label is always show in the header place of SubGrid)

When all lines in one row has set this flag to true there is no empty space show above this lines
